name: Ravi Varma oleograph
summary: A god picture printed by stone lithography in many colours, for the home shrine and the shop wall. The oil-like gloss, the saturated colour and the smooth blend copy the paintings of Raja Ravi Varma.

philosophy.core_thesis: A lithograph in many colours can copy the smooth oil painting of a god and put it in every home for a few annas.
design_principles: Copy a painted original: smooth modelling, a soft light and a figure in the centre.
Print 6–12 stones or plates, one for each colour, in transparent inks that blend.
Use vermilion, ultramarine, gold yellow and a warm flesh tone as the main inks.
Draw a halo, a crown and jewels with a gold-yellow ink and a thin dark line.
Put a plain title in Devanagari or English in a strip at the foot of the sheet.
Finish the sheet with an oil varnish for a deep gloss.
Keep the register within 0.5 mm so that the face and the eyes stay sharp.
anti_patterns: A flat matt colour with no blend
A halftone dot that shows at reading distance
Rough or crude outline of the woodcut kind
A pale pastel palette without a strong red and blue
A sketch line with no painted modelling

process.matrix: Limestone, later grained zinc or aluminium plates, one for each colour.
process.press: A German-made flatbed lithographic press, then an oil varnish on the printed sheet.
process.image_making: A craftsman draws each colour on its stone with crayon and tusche, working from a painted original.
process.edition: Thousands to hundreds of thousands of sheets; the sheets match closely.

inks.strategy: Six to twelve transparent inks that overprint and blend, with a gold yellow for ornament.

colours.name: Deep brown-black
colours.role: the key stone: outline, hair and eyes

colours.name: Vermilion
colours.role: robes, borders and the mark on the brow

colours.name: Ultramarine
colours.role: the skin of Krishna and Vishnu, and the sky

screening.rule: Make the smooth blend with a fine crayon grain on the stone, at about 100 grains an inch, with no visible dot.

registration.rule: Each stone registers to pins; the shift stays at 0.2–0.6 mm and shows as a light rim round the face.

substrate.stock: A smooth, coated or glazed paper, made for colour work and varnished after printing.
substrate.finish: Coated and glazed, with an oil varnish on the face.

surface.impression: No bite: the ink lies on the surface of the coated sheet.
surface.sheen: A deep oil gloss from the varnish, bright on the gold and the red.
surface.texture: A smooth blend with a faint stone grain in the shadows.

emotion.target_response: Warmth and devotion: the viewer sees a bright shrine picture, rich and a little old-fashioned.

avoid_when: The subject is not a devotional or a narrative scene.
The image needs a rough, hand-cut folk line.

modifiers.how: Replace the blend with a thick black outline and flat hand-applied colour on cheap country paper.
Use a Paris poster layout with a large title and a lighter, more decorative figure.
